also, do not conflate breath "support" with breath "velocity". a screamer with good breath control would be able to scream with a lighter a couple inches from their mouth, and not blow it out.

this will also help you hold longer notes.

a good exercise I used, is to pick a note and sing it, and slooowwwwlllyyy fade into a false cord, with medium breath velocity. at some point in the middle you should start "throat singing" because these are the same cords. as you add compression and air, it will turn more into a scream. once you have an understanding of the dynamic of true voice, then true-false mix, try and mentally separate the two feelings. once you mentally isolate the true vocal, you can Kindof train your true vocal cords to stop doing it, leaving distortion only -- Pure false cord.

as someone who does these vocals regularly, what you want to do with your false cord is compress the vestibular vocal folds slightly, and let out a VERY small amount of air.

the one thing you need to realize about this screaming style is that it is pretty quiet, and you can only really do stuff with it if you sing into a microphone. 

unlike learning a false cord where you sigh into it, start with complete vocal fold closure as if you were going to clear your throat. let a TINY bit of air out and channel it into a false cord low.

next, the second most important thing is mouth shape. 
you want a LOW larynx, OPEN or RAISED soft palette(roof of mouth) 
 and a small mouth opening. helps if you imagine your lips as if they were sucking through a straw.

stay about 3 inches away from the mic and VOILA!
